intro: Professionals and everyday users convert terabytes (TB) to gigabytes (GB) when working across metric and metric standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One terabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 gigabytes, while 1 gigabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 terabytes. Whether you are verifying digital storage specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many gigabytes (GB) are in 1 terabyte (decimal) (TB)?
faqs.answer: There are 1,000 gigabytes (GB) in 1 terabyte (decimal) (TB), which rounds to 1,000 GB for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 gigabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 terabytes.

faqs.question: How do I convert terabytes to gigabytes (TB to GB)?
faqs.answer: To convert terabytes to gigabytes, use the formula: GB = TB × 1,000. For example, converting 16 TB gives 16,000 GB.

faqs.question: What is 16 terabytes in gigabytes?
faqs.answer: 16 terabytes (TB) equals exactly 16,000 gigabytes (GB) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
